messages:
alejandro: raising for customer FinPort — they see repeated 429s and billing anomalies after rotating an API key this morning. They run two projects under the same org and egress through a NAT. 429s started ~09:04 UTC.

samir: thanks — can you paste the request headers (sanitized) and a short repro? are they using an org token, project key, or per-project key?

alejandro: short headers: `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>` ; `X-Redwood-Org: org-finport` ; no `X-Redwood-Project` header because they rely on API key to resolve project. After rotation we see the new key accepted but a subset of requests got attributed to IP only.

jess: logging snippet from our auth service shows fallback: `WARN auth: api_key not found -> fallback to ip_scoping (nat=34.120.45.8)` then quota check against scope=ip:34.120.45.8

jess: reproduced locally with a small script that triggers the edge: 
``
# simulate two projects sharing NAT
for i in {1..300}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer KEY-A" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
done &
# rotate KEY-A to KEY-A.new (server-side) and immediately start bursts from KEY-B
for i in {1..300}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer KEY-B" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
done
``

oncall_sre: root cause theory: when key rotation leaves a short window where token lookup returns not-found (race with key propagation), we fallback to IP-based scoping and the per-IP bucket owns the burst -> crossing projects. There's also a TTL on the project binding cache (~30s) which amplifies impact.

mike: is this the known "affinity fallback" behavior? iirc we prefer api_key > project header > ip. If api_key lookup fails we fall back to ip for availability. But that causes billing and quota issues.

alejandro: customer says they did rotation with zero-downtime mode but they still saw 429s and billing shows tokens charged to org-level rather than project-level usage.

samir: short term: create an emergency override for project proj-889 to cover today's burst and reset attribution. I'll file support ticket SUP-2026 and request a quota bump.

oncall_sre: longer term fixes: 1) increase key propagation atomicity (avoid not-found window), 2) ensure proxy always forwards `X-Redwood-Project` if present, 3) add a config flag to disallow ip fallback when org/project headers are present (`prefer_auth_only: true`), 4) shorten cache TTL or add jitter/backoff on key-verification failures.

jess: repro steps to hand to infra:
1) setup two projects proj-A and proj-B under org-finport
2) configure both to egress through same NAT 34.120.45.8
3) start sustained 150 RPS from KEY-A for 20s
4) rotate KEY-A to new key but don't warm caches -> generate concurrent 300 RPS from KEY-B
5) observe `auth: api_key not found` logs and 429s attributed to IP bucket

alejandro: customer wants permanent mitigation ASAP. can we patch routing priority? pls advise on ETA for `prefer_auth_only` toggle.

oncall_sre: we can ship a toggle to keystone config next week; hotfix to increase propagation/consistency might take 3 days. For now: (a) manual quota reassign, (b) ask customer to add explicit `X-Redwood-Project` header while rotating keys, (c) recommend rolling rotation with overlap window.

mike: i've added notes to the incident runbook and linked logs: https://internal.redwood/ingest/log/2023/1759994321

rate-limiter-bot: Rate limiter triggered: ip:34.120.45.8 window=60s burst=500 -> blocked=372

alejandro: thanks all — i'm sending repro + logs to infra + cc'ing customer's eng. I'll keep thread updated with SUP-2026 ticket.
